$comment: NREG-01 default-path regression baseline (Phase 18 Plan 01, Task 3). Authored by hand from a documented pre-Phase-18 (Phase 17 ship) review run against a single-file PR carrying one P0 finding + one P2 finding + a walkthrough comment. The test/rounds-default-bytes-identical.spec.ts spec runs the Phase 18 code with rounds.incremental:false for both round 1 (fresh PR) and round 2 (prior anchor) and asserts the EXTERNALLY-VISIBLE payload (submitReview body shape, walkthrough body shape, severity counts, comment count + order, token totals, file selection) matches this fixture. Do NOT regenerate this fixture from the implementation under test -- the whole point is that it was captured from a pre-Phase-18 implementation, so a future regression is caught by byte-equality drift.

round1.$comment: Review 1 of a fresh PR: round = 1, mode = 'full'. The submitReview body shape and walkthrough body shape are byte-equivalent to the Phase 17 baseline.

round2.$comment: Review 2 of the same PR after a prior finalize: round = 2, mode = 'fallback' (because rounds.incremental:false makes the consumer paths inert even when the anchor exists). Externally-visible payload matches round 1 byte-for-byte -- the ONLY differences are jobs.review_round (2 vs 1), jobs.review_mode ('fallback' vs 'full'), and the rounds.detected audit event payload.

consumerPathInvariants.$comment: rounds.incremental:false MUST keep consumer paths inert (no compare-diff call, no thread listing, no floor escalation beyond the user's setting). These are the load-bearing NREG-01 invariants the default-disabled reviews preserve.
